professional_experience.title: Cloud Consultant - Professional Services (DevOps/MLOps)
professional_experience.summary: Assisting enterprise customers in designing, migrating, implementing, and building scalable solutions on AWS with infrastructure automation and MLOps.

description.1: Accounts were created by a legacy pipeline and the landing zone had no infrastructure as code. I built it in Terraform: Organizations OUs with Control Tower baselines, SCPs and tag policies, and an account baseline that gives every account OIDC deploy roles and a security baseline (IMDSv2, EBS encryption, public-access blocks, no default VPC). 4,000+ resources across 20+ Terraform Cloud workspaces with none failing, and per-account setup cut ~90% (3+ days to under 4 hours).
description.2: Every new VPC, route and firewall rule needed a network-team ticket. I built two Transit Gateway hubs in separate AWS Regions with Network Firewall inspection, VPN and Direct Connect, plus self-service onboarding: each new workload gets its own route table within 15 minutes and firewall access by tag in about a minute.
description.3: Backup, patching and access were set up account by account. I moved them into code: AWS Backup with a delegated-admin vault and SSM Patch Manager in every workload account, and IAM Identity Center permission sets with least-privilege deploy roles.
description.4: AWS IPAM had been ruled out on cost. I measured real billing in a sandbox, showed that prefix delegation cut the projected cost by about 94%, and the customer approved it; a multi-level IP pool tree is now live.
description.5: Every production change goes through the customer's change control and is applied by their engineers. I mirrored the estate in a sandbox so each change runs there first through the same least-privilege role, and brought console-made changes into Terraform without a single diff.
description.6: Faster delivery: a second landing zone foundation stood up in about four weeks, ahead of schedule; a blocker on a private Kubernetes endpoint was fixed the next day with a self-hosted Terraform agent; a hybrid network link went live in one day; reusable Terraform modules replaced copied code. Kiro and Claude Code drove the specs and 50+ design documents with 130+ architecture figures.

case_study.problem: The customer needed a landing zone built as code for two migration programmes at once: accounts came from a legacy pipeline, nothing was in Terraform, and every VPC and firewall rule was a network-team ticket.
case_study.built: Terraform automation for the whole foundation: guardrails, account baselines, Identity Center, backup and patching, two Transit Gateway hubs, IPAM, and self-service network onboarding.
decisions: A separate network hub per programme, sharing one module library
Tag-driven firewall access through hub-owned prefix lists and one writer
AWS IPAM with prefix delegation, enforced by a narrow SCP
Every change applied in a sandbox mirror first, same least-privilege role
case_study.outcome: Per-account setup went from 3+ days to under 4 hours (~90% faster), migrations landed on a fully coded foundation (4,000+ resources, none failing), and new workload networks onboard in minutes.

Blue-green endpoint deployment with auto-scaling and drift detection
CloudFront frontend with an API Gateway and Lambda inference API
case_study.outcome: The endpoints support zero-downtime model updates with automatic rollback, and the work was generalized and published by AWS as an official sample under aws-samples (MIT-0).
